setup_summary.text: UNH reports fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-01-25 after the close. Consensus is EPS $2.29 and revenue $113.43B. The stock has averaged a ±8.1% closing move over the last 8 reports. It has 3 beats and 1 miss in the last 4 quarters, with an average surprise of +12.3%. The consensus basis (GAAP vs adjusted) is not stated.

The Q3 print is already out (Oct 13), so the Q2 10-Q is stale as a baseline. Q3 revenue was $112.7B vs $113.2B. Earnings from operations were $6.56B vs $4.32B. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.56 vs $2.59, and adjusted EPS was $4.69 vs $2.92. Management raised full-year guidance.

Guidance sets a low Q4 bar. Adjusted EPS of at least $20.50 less $18.30 through nine months implies Q4 adjusted EPS of about $2.20 or more. GAAP of at least $19.50 less $17.50 implies about $2.00 or more. Consensus of $2.29 is only about 4% above the adjusted floor.

The year-ago Q4 comp is unusually weak. FY2025 earnings from operations of $18.96B less $18.58B for the first nine months leaves about $0.38B in Q4 2025. FY2025 diluted EPS of $13.23 less $13.21 for nine months leaves roughly $0.02. Q4 2025 carried $2.5B of restructuring and other actions, including a $623M loss-contract reserve. The fact-sheet '-11.7% y/y' EPS growth compares consensus with Q3 2025 EPS of $2.59, not Q4 2025.

Margins peaked in Q2 and stepped down in Q3. MCR rose from 86.7% in Q2 to 88.4% in Q3 (89.9% a year ago). Earnings from operations fell from $7.99B to $6.56B. The CFO flagged that utilization typically steps up in the back half.

Q3 MCR was helped by $610M of net favorable reserve development. That is about 0.7 points on $87.1B of premiums, so ex-release MCR was roughly 89.1% (my arithmetic). The release ties this development to 2026 dates of service, so the label differs from the prior-year development framing used in the 10-Q.

Earnings recovery is margin-led, not growth-led. Q3 revenue fell 0.4% y/y. UnitedHealthcare served 48.3M people vs 50.1M a year ago, and Optum Health revenue fell 10%. Optum Rx adjusted scripts were 393M vs 414M.

Cash flow and balance sheet. Nine-month operating cash flow was $25.1B vs $18.6B. Debt-to-capital was 41.7% vs a roughly 40% year-end target. Moody's, S&P and Fitch all carried Negative outlooks at June 30.

Street positioning. The stock closed at $406.97 on Oct 30 against a consensus price target of $478.68 (+17.6%). Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Mizuho, RBC, Bernstein, JPMorgan, Piper and Barclays maintained positive ratings in October. TD Cowen is at Hold and Baird at Neutral.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.69 vs $2.92 a year earlier (GAAP $4.56).

consensus.text: Consensus EPS $2.29 (basis not stated), against a guide-implied floor of about $2.20 adjusted.

view.text: The bar is the guide floor of about $2.20, with consensus just above it. The EPS step-down from $4.69 is explained by management as Q4 utilization seasonality, Optum Health risk seasonality and added tech/AI/clinician-workflow investment. Three raises this year and a Q3 beat of about $0.57 vs $4.12 argue the floor is conservative. Q3 also leaned on a $610M release that may not recur, so model Q4 off MCR, not off the Q3 run-rate.

consensus.text: Consensus $113.43B, about +0.2% vs Q4 2025's roughly $113.2B (FY2025 $447.57B less nine months $334.35B).

view.text: Consensus needs about +0.7% sequential growth from Q3's $112.69B while UnitedHealthcare membership, Optum Health value-based revenue (-10% y/y in Q3) and Optum Rx scripts are all shrinking. Revenue is a modest risk to the downside. Pricing and Medicaid rates are the offsets.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 MCR 88.4% (Q2 86.7%, Q3 2025 89.9%), including $610M of net favorable reserve development.

view.text: Expect Q4 above Q3's 88.4%. Q3 ex-release was roughly 89.1%, management flagged a back-half utilization step-up, and Humana cites lower favorable reserve development in 2026. The y/y comp is easy: Q4 2025 MCR was about 92.4% (my arithmetic from FY and nine-month medical costs and premiums), including a $623M loss-contract reserve. This is the single biggest swing factor for the EPS print.

Management plans accelerating investment in technology, processes and people in the final months. The ratio is likely at or above 12.8%. The Q4 2025 base was about 15.0% because of restructuring and other charges (my arithmetic).

since_filing.text: Q3 beat and raise (Oct 13). Adjusted EPS was $4.69 vs a $4.12 consensus, and revenue $112.7B vs about $111.0B expected. MCR was 88.4% and the operating cost ratio 12.8%.

The 10-Q said the Q2 MCR improvement was driven by favorable prior-period reserve development ($1.25B in the first half). For Q3, the release attributes $610M of net favorable development to 2026 dates of service. The framing differs, so quality-of-beat comparisons across quarters are not like for like. The newer release is for Q3 only and does not overwrite the 10-Q figures.

Medicare Advantage: the 10-Q and 10-K said MA membership would contract through 2026. People served rose to 7.605M at 9/30 from 7.565M at 6/30 (the newer release), though still down from 8.445M at year-end 2025 (the company cites 935K contraction including complex-population programs).

Medicaid tone improved. The 10-Q (Aug 10) warned of continued downward pressure on margins and an insufficient rate environment. On the Oct 13 call management called Medicaid stable through the back half, with good improvement in Q3. Medicaid members still fell by 85K in Q3.
Optum Health revenue decline accelerated from -5% in Q2 to -10% in Q3 as value-based patients fell, while margin improved to 3.2%.

Medicare Advantage 2027 Stars: at least 69% of members are in 4+ Star plans, in line with expectations. Management expects to approach 75% as it moves through 2027 and into 2028, vs an industry average of 70%, and says Stars investment accelerates into Q4 and 2027.

Analyst moves after the print: RBC raised its PT to $498 (Outperform; stock +3.5% on Oct 25 as managed care rallied). JPMorgan raised to $524 (Overweight). Morgan Stanley went to $531 from $529 (Overweight). Bernstein reiterated Outperform at $512. Raymond James cut its PT to $450 from $475 (Outperform). The stock closed at $406.97 on Oct 30.

Peer read-across. Elevance's Q3 benefit expense ratio was 90.6% (-70 bp). Commercial trend is elevated at low double digits but in line with pricing. Medicaid beat on rate actions, with 2026 viewed as the margin trough. Elevance's beat included about $1.85/share of net non-operating benefit, and its shares fell as investors questioned the quality of earnings.

Centene expects MA membership to decline in 2027 as it reshapes its footprint for margin. Humana's Q2 benefit ratio rose to 91.2% from 89.9%, partly on lower expected favorable prior-period reserve development in 2026. Humana reports Q3 on Nov 6, before UNH's Jan 25 print.
A Wells Fargo price-target cut to $487 was reported on 2026-10-27, but the article body carries an October 2023 date, so it is not relied upon. Wells Fargo's Overweight was maintained on 2026-10-27.

The 2027 outlook is likely to land before the Q4 print. Management promised a fuller update 'before the end of the year' and a meeting with investors. By Jan 25, the Q4 report will largely test Q4 delivery against a 2027 framework already on the table.
The Q3 effective tax rate was about 22.2% (provision $1,224M on pretax $5,524M) vs 18.6% in Q2.

key_debates.question: Is the Q4 guide a sandbag, or does the earnings run-rate fall as sharply as guidance implies?

bull.text: The guide floor implies only about $2.20 of adjusted EPS in Q4 vs $4.69 in Q3. UNH has raised three times this year, beat Q3 by about $0.57, and management calls at least $20.50 'a solid run rate'. Q4 2025 earnings from operations were only about $0.38B, so the y/y comp is easy.

bear.text: Management itself flagged a Q4 utilization step-up, Optum Health risk seasonality (a meaningfully negative Q4 implied) and added AI/technology investment. Q3 MCR included $610M of favorable development that may not repeat, and peers cite fading releases.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 MCR vs Q3's 88.4% and the Optum Health Q4 result. Any reserve release in Q4 vs the $610M in Q3 also shows how much of the recovery is operational.

key_debates.question: How durable is the margin recovery: operations or reserve releases and non-operating items?

bull.text: Management attributes the lower MCR to medical cost management, benefit design and pricing discipline. Days claims payable held at 47.0 (46.2 a year ago), which argues against under-reserving.

bear.text: The Q3 MCR beat leaned on $610M of releases (about 0.7 points of MCR). Elevance's Q3 beat contained about $1.85/share of non-operating benefit and its stock fell, so UNH's Q4 faces the same quality-of-earnings scrutiny.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The size of Q4 favorable development, whether DCP holds around 47, and an adjusted-vs-GAAP bridge with few one-offs.

key_debates.question: Can earnings grow in 2027 while membership shrinks?

bull.text: Management sees the low end of 13%-16% growth as a starting point on at least $20.50, which would be about $23.15. That is above a roughly $22.61 consensus. Tailwinds cited: buybacks, value-based care improvement, AI productivity and Optum Health targeting a 6%-8% margin by 2028.

bear.text: People served are down 1.8M y/y and revenue is flat. 2027 brings plan exits (UHC PPOs), Medicaid OBBB reforms phasing in from 2027-2030, investment ramps at UnitedHealthcare and Optum Insight, and pressured benefit funding. Commercial margin recovery is stretching out.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The 2027 outlook (before year-end), AEP results and the commentary on Jan 25 on investment spend and MA growth.

key_debates.question: Are medical cost trends stabilizing or accelerating into year-end?

bull.text: The UnitedHealthcare CEO says no acceleration: commercial is stabilizing at north of 11%, government programs are moderating, and 2027 pricing assumes persistence. Elevance describes commercial trend as stable and in line with pricing.

bear.text: Commercial trend is above the initial 11% expectation. No Surprises Act awards can reach nearly 6% of medical spend in some regions and run 10-11x Medicare rates. Medicaid elevated trend persists in behavioral health, specialty pharmacy and HCBS. The CFO warned back-half utilization steps up.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 commercial and Medicaid MCR, the early read from Humana's Nov 6 report, and any change in the 2027 trend assumptions.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Q4 adjusted EPS lands well above $2.29 as MCR holds near Q3 levels with additional favorable development. Optum Health loses less than implied. The 2027 outlook, shared before the print, anchors at or above 13% growth on a raised 2026 base. Guidance floor is lifted again.

triggers: Q4 MCR at or below about 88.4%
Optum Health Q4 earnings near breakeven or better
Medicaid margin above the 'moderately better than -1%' range
2027 outlook at or above roughly $23.15 adjusted EPS

description.text: Q4 adjusted EPS lands roughly at the $2.20 floor to modestly above the $2.29 consensus. MCR steps up from Q3 as the reserve release fades and utilization rises seasonally. The operating cost ratio holds at or above 12.8% on investment, and Optum Health posts a seasonal loss. Revenue is about flat y/y and FY adjusted EPS finishes at roughly $20.50-$20.80.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Q4 adjusted EPS comes in below the $2.20 floor implied by guidance, as trend accelerates, reserve releases dry up and Optum Health's seasonal loss deepens. Revenue misses on membership and value-based contraction, and the 2027 framing leans on cost cuts rather than growth. The stock, down about 10% over three months into the print on membership concerns, reacts at the high end of its ±8.1% typical move.

triggers: Commercial trend above the north-of-11% level or unfavorable development
New adverse DOJ, RADV or IRS developments

claim.text: Reserve development fading. Q3's MCR included $610M of net favorable development. Humana cited lower expected favorable development in 2026, and UNH's FY2025 favorable development was only $140M. A smaller Q4 release would raise MCR against a low EPS bar.

Commercial cost trend and the No Surprises Act dispute process. Trend is above the 11% initial expectation, with arbitration awards of 10-11x Medicare rates and up to nearly 6% of medical spend in some regions. Recovery to target commercial margins is being pushed out.

Medicaid funding timing. State rate updates lag acuity, and elevated behavioral, pharmacy and home-health costs persist. OBBB reforms phase in 2027-2030. Core margin is only 'moderately better than -1%' in 2026.

Medicare Advantage funding and 2027 membership. The 2027 Final Notice moved toward but stays below forward trend, and risk model revisions continue. Membership is down 935K since year-end 2025, and 2027 plan exits and AEP outcomes are unknown.
Optum Health execution. Revenue fell 10% in Q3 as the unit exits sub-scale value-based markets, and earnings implied for Q4 are meaningfully negative. The margin is 3.2% vs the 6%-8% 2028 target.

IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment (March 2026) seek to significantly increase taxable income for 2017-2020 on intercompany transfer pricing with a foreign subsidiary, and could extend to later years. UNH disputes them and says reserves are adequate. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $5.6B at year-end 2025.

DOJ False Claims Act risk-adjustment suit is unresolved (Special Master favored UNH; DOJ objected), and RADV audits could cause retrospective payment adjustments. Press coverage names the DOJ action as an overhang for 2027.

Leverage and credit ratings. Debt-to-capital of 41.7% is above the 40% target, and Moody's, S&P and Fitch carry Negative outlooks. Continued buybacks and the $1.5B deferred payment for the July acquisition compete for cash.

Portfolio and non-operating noise. The South American sale is still pending, with incremental losses of $76M in Q3 and $209M over nine months. Restructuring, divestiture and equity valuation items move GAAP and adjusted EPS apart. Adjusted EPS runs above GAAP ($18.30 vs $17.50 for nine months).

questions_for_management.question: How much of the step-down from Q3's $4.69 to a guide-implied Q4 of about $2.20 reflects seasonality, investment, reserve assumptions and tax?

why.text: The guide floor implies a steep sequential decline, and management attributes it to utilization seasonality, Optum Health seasonality and investments, without quantifying them.

questions_for_management.question: What exactly is the $610M of favorable development 'related to 2026 dates of service', and does the Q4 outlook assume further releases?

why.text: The release wording differs from the 10-Q's prior-year development framing, and the item moved Q3 MCR by about 0.7 points. Peers expect lower favorable development.

questions_for_management.question: What is the expected Q4 Optum Health earnings loss, split between risk seasonality and discretionary investment?

why.text: An analyst noted that full-year Optum Health guidance implies a meaningfully negative Q4, while management says Q3 performance is durable.

questions_for_management.question: How should we think about 2027 revenue and membership given Medicare Advantage plan exits, Medicaid attrition and commercial attrition?

why.text: Membership is down 1.8M y/y and the 13%-16% growth framework must be delivered without top-line growth. The press reports plan exits for nearly 1M people across UHC and Humana in 2027.

questions_for_management.question: What assumptions underlie the 2027 commercial price increases, and how much of the No Surprises Act arbitration cost can be recovered?

why.text: Trend is above 11%, 2027 pricing assumes persistence, and long-term commercial margins are being pushed out.

questions_for_management.question: What is the exposure and the reserve position on the IRS transfer-pricing proposals, and what tax rate is embedded in Q4 and 2027?

why.text: The Q3 effective rate was about 22.2%, and the NOPAs could extend beyond 2020.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q4 buyback pace, given debt-to-capital at 41.7% against the 40% target?

why.text: Year-to-date buybacks were $5.0B (including a $2.0B forward settled July 1), dividends will exceed $8B, and leverage is still above target with negative rating outlooks.

data_gaps: The Q3 2026 10-Q was not among the filings read. Q3 figures come from the 8-K release and call, so the medical costs payable rollforward, reserve development tables and updated legal disclosures for Q3 are unverified.

The basis of the $2.29 Q4 consensus (GAAP vs adjusted) is not stated, and no consensus for segment earnings, MCR or membership was found. The fact-sheet 'Q4 EPS growth -11.7%' uses Q3 2025 EPS ($2.59) as the year-ago base.
Q4 2025 adjusted EPS and adjusted segment results are not in the sources. The Q4 2025 comparisons here are derived from FY2025 less nine-month figures.
The prior GAAP EPS guidance range is not in the sources. The prior adjusted range ($19.50-$20.00) comes from press coverage rather than a company document.
No detailed breakdown is available of the $610M of favorable reserve development by segment or period, or of the receivable-sale contribution to Q3 operating cash flow.

Whisper EPS and the options-implied move are not available (report date is 85 days away). The Q4 consensus snapshot is undated within the 14-day window, so analyst revisions after the Q3 print are not captured.
The Wells Fargo price target cut to $487 comes from an article whose body is dated Oct 2023. The date is unverified and the target is not relied upon.
The 2027 guidance timing is only 'before year-end'. Whether it comes via a separate investor event or 8-K is unknown.
Humana's Q3 report (Nov 6) has not occurred. Texas AG, OIG upcoding and other regulatory news was older than 14 days and is not used as a claim.
